correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the 12-vertex, 18-edge truncated-tetrahedral graph and Abrams ordered disjoint-closed-cell model: 132 zero-, 360 one-, 234 two-cells, no higher cells. The inspected verify.py explicitly constructs the signed 360x234 product boundary. A 214-pivot nonzero minor modulo 1000003 lower-bounds rational rank by 214; 20 linearly independent boundary-zero integral products of disjoint simple graph cycles upper-bound rank by 234-20=214, hence H_2(Q) has dimension 20. Every signed action of the 24 S4 permutations and particle exchange on oriented squares is computed using the free-coordinate kernel basis; modular traces lift uniquely to rational integral characters because finite-order operators have integer traces between -20 and 20. The classwise traces (g,g*tau) are (20,0),(6,-2),(0,-4),(2,0),(0,0); weighted S4 irreducible inner products give exactly claimed decompositions. The two-sided rank sandwich, not a modular rank assumption, is essential. Sufficient-subdivision holds for this simple triangle-girth graph with degree-three vertices. No torsion statement for lower homology or integral S4-module classification is inferred.
residual_risks: The 214-pivot and 20 independent-cycle calculation was checked against complete source algorithm and mathematical rank sandwich, not replayed as a second complete 360x234 numerical computation; an independent execution of exact verifier is a remaining reproducibility step.
Sufficient-subdivision homotopy equivalence and its equivariant naturality are classical topological inputs; exact claimed integral lattice action is not assessed.

value.rationale: A complete symmetry-character classification refines the classical rank-20 graph-configuration homology for a highly symmetric, natural finite graph. It is potentially useful for equivariant graph-braid topology and distinguishes exchange-even and exchange-odd actions, not only a decorative finite count; the exact 20-dimensional character is not implied by the matching-complex or BM tables read.
residual_risks: One particular finite graph rather than a parametrized family; value is the natural symmetry of a canonical Archimedean graph and the ordinary ordered configuration functor.

final_claim: For the ordered two-particle configuration space of the truncated-tetrahedral graph, H_2(X;Q)^+ = 1+2V+V′ and H_2(X;Q)^- = 2*1+2V+W as rational S4 modules, both ten-dimensional, with respective characters (10,2,-2,1,0) and (10,4,2,1,0).
limitations: Rational H2 only for the ordered two-particle truncated-tetrahedral configuration; no lower torsion or integral module normal form.
